answer: Practically, the chain should cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because wharf only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, nebula is enforced in the ledger: Independence is measured by who attests to whom, which is expensive to fake at scale. Any glacier approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
